text:
sam: quick sync — we need to settle on an eviction retry budget and what telemetry is required to validate it across multi-region active/active. hitting noisy evictions in eu-west during promo spikes.
anya: +1. can we define a simple SLA: e.g., max 3 evictions per tenant per hour before failover to standby region?
kevin: prefer an exponential backoff with capped retries rather than a hard count. 3 retries with backoff windows 1m, 3m, 10m seems reasonable.
mira: important: for data residency tenants we can’t failover to a non-resident region. so eviction policy must be residency-aware and expose a different path (throttle vs failover).
sam: yes — two modes: residency-strict => degrade/queue within region; residency-flex => failover allowed. need telemetry to show how often residency-strict tenants hit the queue and their latency impact.
anya: telemetry proposal: per-tenant counters: eviction_attempts, eviction_success, eviction_backoff_total_seconds, queued_requests_count, fallback_failures. tag by region and deployment (dedicated/private/hosted).
kevin: also record lease_reacquire_time and last_leader_heartbeat to diagnose flapping.
infra-bot: deploy scheduled: eviction-metrics-pipeline v1 -> will add eviction_attempts and queued_requests_count. rollout at 02:00UTC. :package:
mira: for residency-strict we should publish a soft-threshold alert when queued_requests_count > 500 across primary region for 5m. that prevents silent quality regressions.
olivia: legal note — when queuing for >30m we might need to notify customers with residency requirements. add a telemetry-derived alert that surfaces tenant IDs hitting >30m queue.
sam: implementation sketch: config snippet below for per-tenant policy (will live in tenant manifest):
```
"eviction_policy": {
  "mode": "residency-strict|residency-flex",
  "retry_budget": 3,
  "backoff_seconds": [60, 180, 600],
  "max_queue_seconds": 1800
}
```
kevin: question — should retry_budget live on route or tenant level? route gives more flexibility for bursty endpoints. leaning route-level override with tenant default.
anya: agree. default at tenant, override at route. makes canarying easier.
mira: ops playbook: 1) if queued_requests_count > threshold, enable preemptive cache-warm and increase KV cache TTL for that tenant; 2) if still failing, notify oncall and run failing-tenants-script to surface top clients.
sam: good. next: how do we validate the safety of failover for residency-flex tenants? propose a simulation harness that replays traffic into standby region using anonymized traces and checks quality + p99 latency delta.
olivia: and add a consent flag in tenant manifest for allowed-failover=true. must be explicit.
kevin: telemetry acceptance criteria: we need histograms of time-to-first-success after eviction, p95/p99 for queued and non-queued, and a daily churn report of tenants moved off primary due to evictions.
anya: action items:
- infra: roll metrics pipeline (infra-bot said deploy) -> @infra-bot follow up when live
- eng-runtime: implement per-tenant manifest + backoff logic (owner: sam)
- eng-sre: create alerts and dashboards for queued_requests_count and >30m queue tenants (owner: mira)
- legal / acct: ensure consent flag phrasing (owner: olivia)
infra-bot: noted. will post when metrics are flowing.
sam: thanks all — let's reconvene after one full day of metrics to pick concrete thresholds. :thumbsup:
